original_question: Can one construct examples of nearly Kahler instantons on the known nearly Kahler 6-manifolds that occur as links of asymptotic cones of asymptotically conical G2-manifolds - namely S^6, CP^3, S^3 x S^3 (and finite quotients), and the flag manifold F2 - and, for any such nearly Kahler instanton, determine whether it occurs as the limit at infinity of a G2-instanton on an AC G2-manifold and, if it does, how many G2-instantons have that prescribed limit?
target_in_paper: §3.3(b), the itemized open problem in the section on asymptotically conical (AC) G2-manifolds, with nearby context from the opening paragraph of §3 and the moduli-space comment in §3.3(c).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s own formulation. It correctly places the question in the AC G2 setting, names exactly the nearly Kähler links listed in the paper (S^6, CP^3, S^3 × S^3 and finite quotients, and the flag manifold F2), asks for construction of nearly Kähler instantons on those links, and then asks the two follow-up questions stated in the paper: whether such nearly Kähler instantons occur as limits at infinity of G2-instantons, and, if they do, how many G2-instantons have that prescribed limit.
missing_details: The paper’s term is 'pseudo-Hermitian–Yang–Mills connection', also called a 'nearly Kähler instanton'; this should be named explicitly.
The nearly Kähler instanton condition should be stated: for the nearly Kähler SU(3)-structure (ω, γ2) on the link M, the limiting connection a satisfies F_a ∧ ω^2 = 0 and F_a ∧ γ2 = 0.
The ambient gauge-theoretic setting should be included: the paper works with connections on principal G-bundles with compact semisimple structure group G.
The AC geometry should be spelled out: X is asymptotic to the cone R_+ × M with the conical G2-structure induced by the nearly Kähler structure on M.
The nearby context only guarantees such a limit for G2-instantons whose curvature decays pointwise at infinity, and even then the paper phrases this as 'if it exists'.
The question should be phrased for the specific links of asymptotic cones of AC G2-manifolds, not for arbitrary nearly Kähler 6-manifolds.
The final 'how many' clause is best understood as fixing a particular nearly Kähler instanton a and asking for the set of G2-instantons having a as asymptotic limit at infinity.

Nearby §3.3(c) shows that this multiplicity question sits inside a natural projection from the moduli space of AC G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kähler instantons; that contextualizes, but does not replace, the narrower open problem in §3.3(b).
refined_question: Let M be one of the known nearly Kähler 6-manifolds that occurs as the link of the asymptotic cone of an asymptotically conical G2-manifold, namely M ∈ {S^6, CP^3, S^3 × S^3 (and finite quotients thereof), F2}. For a principal G-bundle over M with compact semisimple structure group G, can one construct pseudo-Hermitian–Yang–Mills connections a on M (equivalently, nearly Kähler instantons, i.e. connections satisfying F_a ∧ ω^2 = 0 and F_a ∧ γ2 = 0 for the nearly Kähler SU(3)-structure (ω, γ2) on M)? For each such a, does there exist a G2-instanton A on an asymptotically conical G2-manifold asymptotic to the cone on M, with pointwise decaying curvature at infinity, whose limit at infinity is a; and, if so, how many such G2-instantons have a as their asymptotic limit?
justification: The draft is capturing the open problem stated almost verbatim in §3.3(b). The extra precision needed to make it fully stand-alone comes from nearby context: §3 explains that an AC G2-manifold is asymptotic to the cone on a nearly Kähler 6-manifold and that a G2-instanton with pointwise decaying curvature has, if a limit exists, a pseudo-Hermitian–Yang–Mills/nearly Kähler instanton as its limit at infinity. The paper also records concrete asymptotic examples on F2 and on S^3 × S^3, which motivate the broader construction problem. Finally, §3.3(c) shows that the paper views the 'how many' part as a fiber question for a natural projection from the moduli space of AC G2-instantons to the moduli space of nearly Kähler instantons, although the exact target of your draft is the narrower open problem in §3.3(b).
